The vendor case study has no exact event time, and Index Us cannot independently inspect the code, parity harness or customer results.

Current article bodies and records for Harbor, Arm AI Portal, Google's adversarial-AI report and Cisco update, Meta Muse, ChatGPT Images 2.5 and the Codex quantum-lab case were checked; no material correction or duplicate story identity was found.

decision.reason: The exact-timestamped preprint is fresh, consequential and not covered by Index Us. It supports a useful conditional decision: isolated subagents helped only after procedures had explicit input-output contracts, while loose knowledge packages favoured inline execution and subagents added token cost. SkillsBench and peer-reviewed long-context research provide independent context without being presented as confirmation.

claims.text: arXiv's cs.AI RSS timestamped the public announcement of arXiv:2609.09233 at 2026-09-10T04:00:00Z.
claims.sourceLocator: Matching RSS item and pubDate

claims.text: The preprint's v1 submission history records 2026-09-07T20:14:11Z and lists Cornell University and Microsoft Research Cambridge affiliations.
claims.sourceLocator: arXiv metadata, title page and submission history

claims.text: Inline skill execution loads a package's instructions into the main context, while the tested subagent mode starts a separate context with those instructions and returns the worker's final response.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML sections 2 and 3.1; Equations 5-7

claims.text: The experiment used a modified OpenHands harness and the current 87-task SkillsBench family.
claims.sourceLocator: Paper section 4 and Appendix A.3; current SkillsBench registry

claims.text: The researchers ran GPT-5.3 Codex three times on all SkillsBench tasks, collected successful trajectories and used Copilot CLI with minimal human intervention to synthesise contract-driven packages for 64 tasks.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4, Synthesizing procedural skill packages

claims.text: The paper's main execution-mode comparisons use the 64-task subset for which contract-driven packages were produced.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4 immediately before Figure 2

claims.text: The authors state that comparing the original and synthesised package sets is not controlled because their content differs.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4, Main results

claims.text: With original packages that generally lacked explicit input-output contracts, inline skills matched or outperformed subagents across all tested models.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4, Main results and Figure 2

claims.text: With synthesised procedural packages and explicit input-output contracts, subagents outperformed inline execution across the tested models.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4, Main results and Figure 2

claims.text: The paper frames a suitable subagent procedure through invocation conditions, a method and an output contract.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 3.2; Equations 8-10

claims.text: When irrelevant tool descriptions increased context pressure, contract-driven subagent execution degraded more gradually than inline execution.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4; Figures 3 and 6

claims.text: For stronger tested models including GPT-5.3 Codex and Kimi K2.6, subagent execution produced lower peak context on more than 80 per cent of tasks.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4, Peak context length and total token cost; Figure 4

claims.text: The paper reports substantially higher total token use for subagents because information is communicated across separate contexts.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML sections 3.1 and 4; Figure 4

claims.text: The authors caution that peak-context comparisons for weaker models were confounded by early termination of some inline runs.
claims.sourceLocator: HTML section 4, Peak context length and total token cost

claims.text: The SkillsBench launch snapshot began with 86 tasks and reported on 84 after two verifier runtime errors.
claims.sourceLocator: Launch post, benchmark description and evaluation setup

claims.text: SkillsBench reported variable effects by task and domain, with 16 of 84 evaluated tasks showing negative skill effects.
claims.sourceLocator: Launch post, Skills can hurt performance

claims.text: The current SkillsBench site identifies a later v1.1 registry with 87 tasks, so the launch and current snapshots are not interchangeable.
claims.sourceLocator: Launch historical-snapshot note and current registry metadata

claims.text: A peer-reviewed EMNLP 2025 study tested five open- and closed-weight models on mathematics, question answering and coding and reported 13.9-85 per cent declines as input grew despite perfect retrieval and lengths inside advertised limits.
claims.sourceLocator: ACL publication metadata and abstract

claims.text: The ACL finding supports testing context isolation as a mitigation hypothesis but does not establish that subagents solve every long-context problem.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us boundary between independent input-length evidence and the preprint's subagent test

claims.text: The new study is a preprint using one benchmark family, a modified harness, contract packages derived from successful trajectories and deterministic task verifiers.
claims.sourceLocator: arXiv status, paper section 4 and Appendix A.3, and SkillsBench descriptions

claims.text: A defensible deployment choice is to keep loose shared-state guidance inline and trial subagents for substantial procedures expressible through a narrow auditable contract.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us synthesis from conditional execution results, variable skill effects and context-pressure evidence

claims.text: A local comparison should evaluate accepted completion, total cost, latency, hand-off loss, context relief and operational control rather than transfer benchmark accuracy directly.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from the accuracy, context, token and version trade-offs
